{{Strong|''Rosulabryum capillare''}} (formerly ''Bryum capillare'') is a species of [[moss]] in the [[Bryaceae]] family.<ref name="wfo">{{Cite WFO|genus=Rosulabryum |species=capillare |authority=(Hedw.) J.R. Spence |id=0001201518 |access-date=9 February 2024}}</ref> It has [[cosmopolitan distribution]]<ref name="GBIF">{{cite web |title=Bryum capillare Hedw. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/7259189 |website=www.gbif.org |access-date=1 February 2021 |language=en}}</ref> and is known by the [[common name]] {{Strong|capillary threadmoss}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bryum capillare |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/bryum-capillare/ |website=British Bryological Society |access-date=1 April 2023}}</ref>

''Rosulabryum capillare'' can use [[artificial light]] to grow in places that are otherwise devoid of natural light, such as [[Crystal Cave (Wisconsin)|Crystal Cave]] in Wisconsin.<ref name="Thatcher 1949">{{cite journal |last1=Thatcher |first1=Edward P. |title=Bryophytes of an Artificially Illuminated Cave |journal=The Bryologist |date=1949 |volume=52 |issue=4 |pages=212–214 |doi=10.2307/3239480 }}</ref>
